messages:
alana: Quick follow-up from the RFC thread about quant profiles — proposing a small refactor: introduce explicit 'safepoints' for precision switches and centralize operator dispatch.
mike: +1 on having explicit safepoints. can you sketch where these land? layer boundaries? attention blocks?
jess: My gut: layer boundaries only, otherwise KV cache/attention state gets messy. safepoint = after layer norm & before matmuls so we can swap kernels and quant params.
alana: Exactly. proposal: safepoint at two places: (a) post-layer-norm pre-attn, (b) post-attn pre-ffn. That keeps caches consistent and minimizes mid-op state transforms.
zach: How do we implement with our current kernel registry? we have per-op kernels keyed by (op, dtype, hw). Want to avoid combinatorial explosion.
alana: Operator-dispatch table proposal: map (op, safepoint_profile_hint) -> prioritized kernel list. Profile hint is light: {preferred_bitwidths, fallback_order, quant-affinity-tag}. Runtime evaluates hint at safepoint and sets dispatch policy for subsequent ops until next safepoint.
mike: So instead of tagging every op with a profile, runtime sets a transient dispatch context at safepoint. Nice. reduces metadata overhead.
jess: Concern: canarying/rollouts per customer — how do we override dispatch at runtime? per-request headers? endpoint config?
alana: We expose per-endpoint override: endpoint config can include 'precision_policy' which merges into dispatch context at safepoint. Also allow token-level hints but only for downstream routing, not kernel switches mid-op.
nisha: Telemetry asks: we need to emit metrics at safepoints — which kernel used, decision latency, and any fallback events. Also sample outputs for HQ QA when fallback from fp8->int8->4bit occurs.
zach: Runtime cost: adding safepoints introduces a tiny scheduling barrier. Have we measured? rough numbers?
alana: Microbench: adding a safepoint check at boundary is ~30-50ns on hot path; kernel selection + context set ~200-500ns one-time per layer boundary. With layers ~24, worst-case ~12ms? No — that's wrong, recalc: 500ns * 48 boundaries = 24us. negligible relative to kernel cost for long sequences.
mike: Thanks for numbers. One more: how do we handle sharded models where chunks of layers live on different devices and dispatch tables must be consistent across devices?
alana: Two options: (1) centralized control plane that pushes dispatch context to all devices before executing next chunk; (2) deterministic policy derived from request metadata so each device independently computes same dispatch (no roundtrip). prefer #2 for latency.
jess: Deterministic policy needs stable inputs: model version, endpoint precision_policy, and a small per-request seed (e.g., customer override). That should be reproducible across devices.
zach: What about fallback safety: if a kernel fails at runtime (e.g., OOM or precision assert), we need an atomic fallback to a safe kernel and mark telemetry + degrade gracefully.
ops-bot: deploy-note: add alert if fallback-rate > 0.5% over 5m for production endpoints. Paging if >2%.
nisha: For QA: add a regression test harness that exercises all fallback paths with small prompts and compares embeddings/logprobs to golden. Label tests by "safepoint_path" so we can replay exact dispatch traces.
mike: API ergonomics: do we expose precision_profile in the public SDK or keep it internal? I vote internal with opt-in flags for advanced users.
jess: Agree. public SDK could accept a friendly string ("size-first", "quality-first") which maps to internal precision_policy.
alana: Implementation plan (short):
  - RFC follow-up PR: add safepoint markers into compiler IR + runtime boundary hooks (2w)
  - Dispatch table implementation + lightweight policy merge (2w)
  - Telemetry: safepoint events + kernel tags + fallback counters (1w)
  - QA tests and canary: shadow traffic run + compare outputs, and staged rollout (2w)
Total ~7 weeks for an MVP path.
zach: Can we do an even quicker experiment? runtime flag to force a global dispatch policy (no safepoints) to validate kernels & fallbacks first.
alana: Yes — feature-flagged `--force-dispatch=policyX` to run across all ops. Good for initial perf/sanity runs.
jess: One more operation detail: quant params handshake — we need a stable binary serialization for quant tables so different runtimes can verify compatibility. keep it versioned.
nisha: Add a telemetry tag for quant-table-version at safepoint. helps debugging.
mike: Sounds actionable. who wants the follow-up PRs?
alana: I'll do the compiler IR + runtime hook. zach and jess take dispatch table + kernel registry changes. nisha will spec telemetry + QA harness. mike will own SDK mapping.
jess: I'll sketch the dispatch table layout in PR comments tonight.
zach: I'll prototype the deterministic policy generator for sharded runs.
alana: Great. Let's reconvene after initial PRs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
